The Comparison of the Growth of Arugula, Giant Chard and Radish in Lunar
Regolith and Potting Soil Mixture
Team Name: AVID Curiosity
Team #17489
Culbreth Middle School
Team Members: Jack R, Ashwin P, Avery R, Harmony H, Michelle M, Taliah R, Nathalie H, Reagan
K, Matthew S, Chase H, Caleb R.
Coach: Mrs. Christine Sudzina Schut
Background
The plants chosen for the research are plants that we believe will thrive best in lunar regolith and will also be
the most nutritious, and that is important for astronauts on the moon. Since lunar regolith has no nutrients, we
chose Arugula, Giant Chard and Radishes because they were the healthiest and fastest growing plants that were
found. They give an abundance of vitamins, nutrients and grow within the designated time frame for PTMC.
All of the minimum light, temperature and soil types (for the 3 plants) are similar, making it easy to grow them
together. Arugula may help prevent cognitive decline in humans, lowers the risk of several chronic diseases,
even though it is small and fragile. The Radishes grow quickly and also have a strong scent which repels and
confuses pests, and are a great fill in crop between other longer germinating crops, making them perfect plants
to have once larger fields and crops start to be developed on the moon. Giant Chard will be the plant that will
grow to the fullest, and can be eaten both cooked and uncooked, they also help by providing a great amount
with fibre; just one large leaf has four times the recommended daily amount.
Experimental Design
We used 9 pots that were split into 3 groups. Each group consisted of 3 pots, 2 pots had 60% lunar regolith and
40% earth soil (they were mixed), the final pot (the control) had 100% earth soil. Each pot had 5 seeds placed
4.5cm down in the soil (45 seeds in total). They had 10 hours of light each day from LED lights in a Grow Box.
The plants were given between 10-20 mL of water daily depending on the plants’ conditions. All plants received
the same amount of water to be consistent. Data was collected every Wednesday from the day of planting until
Week 8 when we uprooted the plants and did the final measurements. Pictures were taken several times a week to
track the plants’ growth. To keep light levels and temperature consistent no matter the conditions, grow boxes
were used with LED lights.

Procedure
1. Take pictures of every single step throughout the planting and data collecting process.
2. Set up an air filter near grow boxes.
3. First collect labeling tape (3 colors) and thin sharpie markers.
4. Label containers (remember to set aside one pot as an extra!)
a.
Label the date and name of the plant, group name, and the number of the pot.
5. Put on PPE. (Lab coat, mask, gloves, goggles)
6. Go outside and put 9 pots, 2 spoons, 3 rulers, Fox Farm potting soil and lunar regolith on the metal table.
7. Use a ruler for all measurements; place a ruler with a 0 cm inside and at the bottom of the pot.
8. Using a spoon, put 7cm of potting soil in the 3 control pots. (pot # 1, 4, 7)
9. Using a different spoon, add 4cm of lunar regolith to all other pots. (pot # 2,3,5,6,8,9)
10.
Add 3cm of potting soil to pots with lunar regolith. (pot # 2,3,5,6,8,9)
11.
Mix lunar regolith and potting soil with your gloved hands.
12.
Measure 4.5 cm on your fingers, and use that reference point to make 5 holes in each pot’s soil
regolith mixture using your finger.
13.
Bury 1 seed in each of the holes. (45 # of seeds total 15 of each type.)
14.
When the pots are complete, put the pots in a plastic tray in numerical order.
15.
Wipe down the metal table and make sure no lunar regolith is sticking to anything.
16.
Take all materials and your tray of pots and put the tray into a Carolina Biological grow box.
17.
Set up a mechanical timer to the grow box. (10 hrs of light, goes on at 8am and off at 6pm.)
18.
Water plants. 20 mL water for the first day, 10 mL for days Mon-Fri except for weekends.
19.
On Wednesdays collect data in google docs, as well as take pictures with ipad and camera, (pictures
taken with camera daily) place pictures in a labeled digital folder.
20.
After the end of the 8 weeks harvest the plants and take the last data of the plants including the
length of the roots.
Hypothesis
The essential question is, “What plant will grow the fastest or the best in Lunar Regolith while mixed with
Earth Soil?” Doing research, the three main plants were Radishes, Giant Chard, and Arugula. Based on our
research we believe the Radishes will be the fastest growing, We thought this because Radishes have the fastest
germination time. Giant Chard will grow to be the fullest and the biggest, we thought this because from our

research they seemed to adapt well to harsh environments (Lunar regolith being a harsh environment.) Arugula
will be the smallest and most fragile, because it is a microgreen and even on earth it does not grow very big.
Arugula also has the biggest difference in light, water and nutrient levels compared to the other plants.
Variables
The control will be 3 pots of 100% potting soil (1 pot for each plant type). The independent variable
will be the 3 different types of plants being used, Fordhook Giant Chard, Astro Arugula, and Sora Radishes (2
pots per plant, there will be 1 pot empty in case of emergency). The dependent variable will be the fullness
and overall health of the plant and the growth, including the measurements in how quick the plants also
sprouted. The things measured will be the height, the amount of leaves and the soil saturation.
Measurements & Procedures for Measurements
The steps are very simple but need to be precise, since Lunar Regolith will require you to wear
and act carefully as well, please note this before you start getting involved with Lunar Regolith.
The first step is to wear protective clothing, like PPE. (Lab coats, masks, gloves, and goggles.)
Every person needs to wear this, even if they are getting close or not, every person in the room or
space should wear it, for safety purposes. Each person should have a set of goggles, gloves and
the lab coats, they will need to put each one of them on carefully so you are protected well
enough. Next for the materials, whoever is planting should have a spoon, or at least an item
similar so you can start to prepare to start and add soil plus Lunar regolith in each pot, but in the
right way. They should put as many scoops of Lunar regolith to the first dent of the pot. (4.5 cm)
and then putting earth soil to fill the rest of the space. Next and most importantly, plant the seeds
for the Giant Chard, Radishes, and Arugula, 4.5 centimeters down into the soil. 9 pots in total,
for the planting, and for emergency, have an extra one. (10 pots in total.)
Controls
The control is 100% Earth Soil, these plants are being used as testers for plants to see how the
plants grow in pure Earth Soil. Each plant is being tested in normal conditions but it is also being
tested in different ways. Light levels, temperature, water amount (in milliletres), humidity and
care were all kept at a constant for all plants.
Results

Radishes
On February 14th all plants were very green and strong. On March 6th plant stems were unable
to support the weight of plant leaves, and leaves had started to shrivel up and fall off. We
attempted to add braces made of paper clips however one of the stems snapped and we took the
braces out. After that we upped the water amount for all plants to 15mL of water. The following
week we upped the water to 20 mL for all plants.

Arugula
The Arugula control already started growing after the first week but it took the other Arugula
pots 3-4 weeks to grow. In total, the other pots had two stems (one stem each) and the control
had three stems. The Arugula had 22 leaves in total at the end.
Giant Chard
The control Giant Chard started growing after the first week. It took the other Giant Chard plants
3 weeks to start growing. The control Giant Chard had 15 stems, pot 8 had 5 stems and pot 9 had
10 stems in the end. The Giant Chard ended up being the plants with the best growth with 27 cm,
18 cm and 13 cm by the 8th week.
Analysis & Conclusion
The essential question was, “What plant will grow the fastest or the best in Lunar Regolith while
mixed with Earth Soil?” Knowing this, doing the research, the three main plants were Radishes,
Giant Chard, and Arugula. Based on our research we believe the Radishes will be the fastest
growing. We thought this because Radishes have the fastest germination time.
When this research was done it was found that indeed Radishes where the best and fastest
growing plant, (by week 3 all radish plants had grown) it also shows that it would grow very fast
but also die after short tiny periods (the control died by 8, while the rest of the radishes plant
went stagnant) without water which confused the research in a way that has still been confused
when pulling up the plants, in conclusion the hypothesis was indeed correct as the radishes where
the fastest.
Our hypothesis was Giant Chard will grow to be the fullest and the biggest, we thought this
because from our research, they seemed to adapt well to harsh environments (Lunar regolith
being a harsh environment.)
Giant chard is the most fullest after doing our research and planting, we were correct since the
Giant chard had the most leaves, height, and number of stems, they did grow to the fullest and
with the graphs and information on the top, the Giant chard was indeed successful.
Arugula will be the smallest and most fragile, because it is a microgreen and even on earth does
not grow very big, it also has the biggest difference in light, water and nutrient levels compared
to the other plants.
We came to this hypothesis due to the Arugula being a micro green and it also having the biggest
difference in light, water and nutrient levels. After doing the work and planting on our own and
taking notes, it seemed that we were right. After planting our Arugulas and then the day of taking
them out, (we had on our PPE and materials we had and you should need when planting and
getting near lunar regolith) we took them out and started to note down the leaves, stems, height,
and other information. After our note taking on our plants, we took out a google doc and started
taking down our notes and used a table to graph our results. The graphs above show our results,
the green lines can tell us what our Arugulas have grown in, it shows that the Arugula had the
lowest amount of leaves, stem, and in height, our research helped us expect this and they had the
lowest amount out of all.

Overall Conclusion
In conclusion, we have learned that Radishes grow quickly but are not a stable source of nutrients due to the
fact that they die off very quickly. Additionally, We would recommend that Arugula would not be used as a
reliable source of nutrients. When scientists do decide to grow it on the moon,we recommend it be given
nutrients, soil and light levels as close as possible to that which it has on earth, otherwise as our experiment
showed they will not grow well. Finally, our recommendation is that Giant chard be used as the main crop in
the first attempts to colonize the moon, due to the fact that it grew comparatively quickly and maintained high
growth and leaf levels, meaning that they would provide the most nutrients for Astronauts.
